given: the stock view rendering stock positions after the tracking code has been split
when: the operator views the stock positions
then: the old combined tracking code is no longer displayed anywhere in the stock view, so the batch and serial fields are the only surface for that identity

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 assert the new batch and serial fields render (populated and empty); AC3 asserts the retired combined code is absent. A view could add the new fields while still showing the old combined code alongside them, so this fails independently.

architectural_notes: E2E: the retirement half of the split, verified through the SPA. Because S1 dropped inventory_code from the stock table, app/models/stock.py no longer carries the column and the boundary (app/routes) can no longer serialize it; AC3 asserts the client stock-view component references no combined-code field anywhere. This is a completeness guarantee across the boundary + client contract (no orphaned reference to the retired column), not a new persistence surface. Cross-cutting concern: dead-field removal / contract cleanliness, owned jointly by the boundary serializer (emits no inventory_code) and the client component (renders none). Owner module: client stock-view component + app/routes stock serializer. Verified by a client component test asserting absence and a real-branch integration test that the boundary payload contains no combined-code key.
